objectives.text:
Letter-Sound Group 1: s, a, t, i, p, n

**New Sounds Introduced:**
/s/, /ă/, /t/, /ĭ/, /p/, /n/

**Full Practice Set (Cumulative):**
s, a, t, i, p, n

**Focus:** Produce the correct, most common sound for each letter in the set when shown the grapheme (the letter shape). For example, when shown 'a', the student says /ă/ (as in 'apple'). It is crucial to teach clean sounds (e.g., a crisp /t/ sound, not "tuh").
Independently produce the most common sound for each letter in this cumulative set, when shown its grapheme. Assess without first saying its sound: s, a, t, i, p, n.

curatorBrief.title: Welcome to Letter Sounds: s, a, t, i, p, n
curatorBrief.intent: Introduce Kindergarten students to the letters s, a, t, i, p, n and their target clean phonemes /s/, /ă/, /t/, /ĭ/, /p/, /n/, emphasizing crisp sounds without adding 'uh'.

objectiveBlocks.objectiveText: Letter-Sound Group 1: s, a, t, i, p, n — Produce the correct, most common clean sound for each letter in the set when shown the grapheme.

components.title: Meet the Letters and Sounds
components.intent: Present cards displaying letters s, a, t, i, p, n paired with clear anchor images (sun, apple, tiger, igloo, pan, nest) and phoneme guides highlighting clean, crisp pronunciation.

components.title: Find the Letter Shapes
components.intent: Reinforce grapheme recognition for Group 1 letters s, a, t, i, p, n through visual matching and initial sound-to-letter tasks with spoken tutor support.

components.title: Listen and Say the Sounds
components.intent: Guide students through direct instruction and vocal modeling of continuous sounds and vowels in Group 1, having students speak the pure phonemes aloud into the microphone.

objectiveBlocks.objectiveText: Independently produce the most common sound for each letter in this cumulative set, when shown its grapheme: s, a, t, i, p, n.

components.title: Letter to Sound Challenge
components.intent: Have students independently see graphemes from Group 1 (s, a, t, i, p, n) and say the matching sound aloud or link sounds directly to letter shapes without prior modeling.

components.title: Sound Match Explorer
components.intent: Provide independent oral practice matching spoken Group 1 phonemes to words and letter sounds, reinforcing clean sound identification across the full cumulative set.

finalAssessment.title: Super Sound Check
finalAssessment.intent: Assess students across all six letters (s, a, t, i, p, n) by checking both visual grapheme-to-phoneme recognition and clean sound identification.

cards.title: Sun and Apple
cards.definition: The bright sun makes sss, and red apple says ah!
cards.timelineContext: First sounds to speak and blend
cards.originStory: Letter S curves like a snake, and letter A sits round with a stick.
cards.curiosityNote: Your tongue stays behind your teeth to hiss like sss!
cards.visualPrompt: A cheerful bright yellow sun smiling next to a crisp red apple, with bold lower-case letters 's' and 'a' clearly displayed, clean picture-book art.

cards.title: Tiger and Igloo
cards.definition: Tiger makes a crisp t sound, and igloo says ih!
cards.originStory: Letter T stands tall with cross arms, while letter I wears a dot hat.
cards.curiosityNote: A clean t sound stops fast without adding uh!
cards.visualPrompt: A friendly playful cartoon tiger sitting beside a shiny round ice igloo, with bold lower-case letters 't' and 'i' nearby, soft colorful storybook style.

cards.title: Pan and Nest
cards.definition: The pan makes a popping p, and nest hums nnn!
cards.originStory: Letter P pops with a round bubble, and letter N arches like a door.
cards.curiosityNote: Feel the tiny puff of air when you say p!
cards.visualPrompt: A cute shiny cooking pan next to a warm twig nest with blue eggs, featuring bold lower-case letters 'p' and 'n', bright and simple kindergarten illustration.

data.title: Sound Safari: Phonics 1: Letter-Sound Group 1: s, a, t, i, p, n

problems.question: Which word starts with the sss sound?
problems.rationale: Sun begins with the /s/ sound, making the same hissing sound as a snake. Apple begins with the /a/ sound, and tiger begins with the /t/ sound. Hearing the first sound in sun helps us learn the sound made by the letter S.
problems.teachingNote: Have students stretch out the beginning sound ('ssss-un') with hand motions like a slithering snake to reinforce phonemic awareness.
successCriteria: Identify the initial /s/ sound in a spoken word
Differentiate the /s/ sound from other initial phonemes like /a/ and /t/
problems.subject: LANGUAGE_ARTS

problems.statement: The letter a makes the short /ă/ sound, like in the word apple.
problems.rationale: The letter 'a' is a key vowel in the first letter-sound group and makes the short /ă/ sound heard at the beginning of words like apple, ant, and alligator. Knowing this primary sound helps young readers start blending simple words together. Recognizing this sound is a foundational step in early phonics development.
problems.teachingNote: Have students trace the letter 'a' in the air while saying the short /ă/ sound and making a pretend apple-biting motion.
successCriteria: Identify the primary short sound of the letter 'a'
Connect the letter 'a' to familiar words like apple
problems.subject: LANGUAGE_ARTS

problems.question: Which word starts with the /t/ sound?
problems.rationale: Tiger begins with the crisp /t/ sound made by tapping your tongue behind your front teeth. In contrast, sun begins with the hissing /s/ sound and pig begins with the popping /p/ sound. Practicing the first sound in words helps build strong phonemic awareness.
problems.teachingNote: Have children tap their tongue to the roof of their mouth to feel how the unvoiced /t/ sound pops out without using vocal cords.
successCriteria: Isolate the initial phoneme in spoken words
Identify the target /t/ sound among familiar phonemes
problems.subject: LANGUAGE_ARTS

problems.question: Which word starts with the /p/ sound?
problems.rationale: Pig begins with the /p/ sound, which is made by popping air through your lips. Apple begins with the /a/ sound and sun begins with the /s/ sound. Hearing that quick puff of air helps us know that pig starts with letter p.
problems.teachingNote: Have students place their hand in front of their mouth to feel the small puff of air when producing the unvoiced /p/ sound.
successCriteria: Identify the initial /p/ sound in spoken words
Distinguish the /p/ sound from other Group 1 letter sounds
problems.subject: LANGUAGE_ARTS

problems.question: Which word starts with the /p/ sound?
problems.rationale: Pig begins with the popping /p/ sound made by your lips. Both nose and nest start with the humming /n/ sound made with your tongue. That means pig is the word that belongs in the /p/ sound group.
problems.teachingNote: Have children place a hand in front of their mouth to feel the puff of air for /p/, and touch their nose to feel the buzz for /n/.
successCriteria: Identify the initial /p/ sound in spoken words
problems.subject: LANGUAGE_ARTS

problems.question: Which thing starts with the letter N sound?
problems.rationale: Nest begins with the letter N, which makes the crisp /n/ sound. Pig begins with the /p/ sound, and igloo begins with the short /i/ sound.
problems.teachingNote: Remind learners to press the tip of their tongue against the roof of their mouth to make the clear /n/ sound.
successCriteria: Identify the initial /n/ sound represented by the letter N
Differentiate the /n/ sound from other Group 1 sounds such as /p/ and /i/
problems.subject: LANGUAGE_ARTS
